THERE WHEN COTU WAS FORMED
MAY. 1, 1968
TO GIVE WORKERS ONE VOICE
THERE WHATEVER THE FUTURE HOLDS
It was not always so. Kenya’s trade union history met difficulties created by the British colonial
government to defend settler employers, and prevent organized labour movement. But unity
proved unstoppable. By 1953, as trade union leaders like Makhan Singh, Fred Kubai, Bildad Kaggia
were detained along with Kenyatta, health inspector and master labour leader Tom Mboya filled
the void. In 1965, his protégé, Clement Lubembe became the first Secretary General of COTU as
captured by the Daily Nation and Taifa Leo.
